items.title: RED repro locks the poisoning scenario before any fix
items.context: Un-gameable failing test: submit a quorum at material M1; land a commit that changes materialHash but NOT storyFilesHash; run quorum_submit again. Today the second submit is accepted and the escalation floor then reports every planned round invalid with 'duplicate host/session/key identity'. The RED assertion is that the second submit must be REFUSED while the standing quorum still evaluates ok.
items.userSees: A smoke/unit test that fails on current main by demonstrating the accepted redundant resubmit and the resulting all-rounds-invalid floor collapse.

happy.desc: Submit rounds=3 quorum at M1, commitMainDrift (materialHash changes, storyFilesHash unchanged), call quorum_submit again -> on unfixed code the second submit is accepted and evaluateHostVerdictRounds reports all rounds invalid (duplicate host/session/key identity); RED test asserts the second submit must be REFUSED -> fails on current main, passes after fix; WHY: proves the poisoning scenario is real and the repro is un-gameable

items.title: Align the quorum_submit duplicate guard with the floor's drift-accept predicate
items.context: In handlers/quorum-submit.ts, the guard must treat a committed verdict on a planned runId as colliding when it would be accepted by the floor at evaluation time: same materialDigest OR (stale materialDigest but storyFilesHash equal to the current storyFilesHash). The refusal message must state that the existing quorum still drift-accepts and nothing needs resubmitting.

items.title: Official recovery command for poisoned quorum rounds
items.context: New command (quorum_prune) that, for a story, identifies host_verdict duplicate events on the same runId + host/session/key identity in the committed process-events.jsonl, and removes the losing set (default: the set whose materialDigest no longer resolves; explicit selector otherwise). Must support --dryRun, write a backup of the jsonl before editing, and commit the metadata change. Formalizes the manual B-bf52 surgery (commit 255eefd289).
items.userSees: lattice quorum_prune --storyId=... --dryRun lists the duplicate verdict events and which set would be removed; without --dryRun it backs up, removes them, commits, and the escalation floor returns to the pre-poisoning assurance level.
excludes: any change to floor/escalation acceptance semantics

happy.desc: Inject duplicate host_verdict events on the same runId + host/session/key identity into committed process-events.jsonl (simulating B-bf52 poisoning), run quorum_prune with dryRun:true -> output lists the exact duplicate verdict events (verdictId, runId, host, materialDigest, timestamp) and which set would be removed vs which survives; WHY: validates the discovery and reporting logic

verification.command: node packages/main/dist/tasks/quorum-submit-smoke.js --grep="quorum_prune dry-run lists the poisoned duplicates without mutating"
verification.selector: quorum_prune dry-run lists the poisoned duplicates without mutating

happy.desc: Run quorum_prune with apply:true on the poisoned fixture -> backup file created alongside process-events.jsonl with timestamp in name, duplicates removed from jsonl, metadata committed; then evaluateReviewEscalation returns full-3x2 assurance level (validRoundCount >= 3); WHY: end-to-end recovery path verification
